text:
maya: Heads-up — after the INT8 KV rollout on the smaller A100 slab we started seeing decode flutters on longer chats. Not huge errors but p95/p99 spike and a couple of hallucination reports.

sam: Which slab/region? any recent kernel swaps?

maya: prod-2 A100-80GB. We auto-switched kernel to int8_fast for KV to save memory. Kernel selection log shows fallback to fast path at ~prep time.

alex: Can you paste the profiler output? curious about cross-device memcpy vs compute.

maya: Pasted below — this is the 30s trace during a repro run: 

```
KV-cache bytes (orig FP16): 18.2GB -> INT8: 4.6GB (compressed)
Batching: avg requests/batch 3.1 -> 2.4 after warmup
p50 token latency: 12.4ms -> 12.0ms
p95 token latency: 48.9ms -> 68.3ms
p99 token latency: 112.5ms -> 188.7ms
CPU memcpy time + kernel selection overhead: +35ms on p95 windows
decode perplexity (eval set): 10.7 -> 12.9
nudge-delta (QA prompts): 6% more factual errors
```

maya: Note p95/p99 went up a lot even though p50 improved slightly. Memory saved is nice but tail latency is painful.

priya: Interesting — looks like batching got worse after compression. Could be KV warmup and cache miss amplification when entries are compressed/packed.

sam: Do we see more page faults or GPU memory stalls? bench-bot, can you run the KV access heatmap on that run id 2022-11-07-xyz?

bench-bot: heatmap job queued: job/kv-heat-222111 -> live in ~7m. Will attach results.

alex: My hypothesis: int8 path uses a different packing layout that increases the number of contiguous memcpy ops for long histories, causing more memcpy scheduling jitter and hurting small-batch decode. Also kernel selection logic may be triggering additional validation/calibration checks on first decode after a model pin.

maya: We tried forcing kernel=int8_dedicated instead of int8_fast and saw p95 drop to ~82ms (still worse than FP16) but p50 nearly same. Switching back to FP16 KV restores p99~115ms.

priya: Do you have traces for KV hit-rate and cold-entry decode overhead?

maya: KV hit rate stayed ~97%, but the *effective* latency per KV lookup doubled for long sequences (lookups requiring unpack+dequantize). The int8 path does unpack + CUDA kernel dequantize per lookup, and that shows up on the profiler as small kernels fired per token (~0.4ms each) which add up at tail.

sam: So it's not network or system mem; it's the per-lookup work and scheduling. Batching heuristic: we used dynamic batching with max-delay 12ms which assumed faster KV paths. With slower per-lookup ops, the heuristic is underbatching.

alex: Two action items: 1) try increasing max-delay to let batches absorb the dequantize overhead, 2) evaluate a hybrid path where only recently-accessed KV entries remain FP16 and older entries use INT8 compression.

priya: Also try changing kernel-selection threshold: prefer int8_dedicated for long-seq callers. We can add a heuristic: if avg_history_len > 64 -> prefer FP16 or int8_dedicated.

maya: Quick experiment results (local):

```
config A: int8_fast + max-delay 12ms -> p99 188ms
config B: int8_fast + max-delay 40ms -> p99 126ms (p50 12.1ms)
config C: int8_dedicated + max-delay 12ms -> p99 82ms
config D: fp16_kv + max-delay 12ms -> p99 115ms (mem +13GB)
```

maya: Config B helps tail a lot but increases avg batch latency slightly. Config C seems best tail-wise but loses most memory savings.

sam: For production we might roll a two-tier KV policy: keep hot-window FP16 (e.g., last 256 tokens) and compress older entries to INT8 slab; add fast-path dequantize fusion in kernel to reduce per-lookup launches.

alex: Agree — also we should add a metric in console: "dequantize-kernel-count-per-request" and surface it on per-route dashboard.

priya: I'll prototype hot-window hybrid compression in the runtime this week. If we can keep the last ~K tokens in cached FP16 view, we can preserve tail quality and still cap memory.

maya: FYI found one decode-quality quirk: certain rare tokens (long numeric sequences) decode differently after quantized KV due to rounding during dequantize; causes small shift that triggers different beam choices. Not frequent but explains hallucination correlation.

sam: Good catch. Let's make an eval set of these edge-case prompts and run regression alerts when quantized-KV changes cross threshold.

bench-bot: heatmap results uploaded: job/kv-heat-222111 -> /artifacts/kv-heat-222111.png (shows many small kernels spiking during tail requests).

alex: TL;DR: INT8 KV saves memory but increases per-lookup kernel launches, hurting p95/p99. Short-term mitigation: increase batching delay and prefer int8_dedicated or hybrid hot-window. Medium-term: fuse dequantize into main decode kernel and adjust kernel selection heuristics by avg_history_len.

maya: I'll open a PR for hybrid hot-window + config guardrails and add a canary on prod-2 with increased max-delay. tagging @sam @priya for review.

sam: LGTM. If hybrid looks good, we can keep memory savings while getting p99 back under SLO. :thumbsup:

priya: I'll add the eval regression set and a dashboard panel for dequantize kernel counts.

maya: Thanks all — will post canary results in this thread.
